| Weight | 2.43lbs / 1.10kg | 2.65lbs / 1.20kg | 2.65lbs / 1.20kg | 
Asus Zenbook 14 (2026) review: Design
- Light and strong body
- Unique finish
- Reasonable port selection
The unique Ceraluminum body certainly sets the Zenbook 14 apart, as do the bright colorways. The beige finish of my review unit was more interesting than the usual monochromatic shades we’ve grown accustomed to, looking softer and more inviting as a result. This was further aided by the rounded corners and the odd texture of the material, which has a slight graininess that’s comfortable in the hand.
One of the major selling points of the Zenbook 14’s construction is its lightness. It weighs around 2.5 pounds (just over a kilogram), which is impressive for a 14-inch laptop. However, it’s not quite as thin as you might expect, with a bit more unexpected bulk at the rear. The two long bars that run underneath, acting as feet, don’t help matters, either.
However, some may view this a worthy sacrifice for the unit’s surprising solidity. Both the base and the lid have very little flex to them. It feels slightly sturdier than the A14 I reviewed previously, although that model is slightly lighter at 2.16 lbs / 0.98kg.
There is, though, one weak point to the Zenbook 14’s build, and unfortunately that’s the keyboard. Hammering away on the keys often depresses the whole board, which can be quite annoying and doesn't inspire much confidence. There’s also no backlighting, which is an omission I always lament.
On the plus side, there are a reasonable number of ports on the Zenbook 14. There’s one USB-A port on the right-hand side of the unit, which is the only port on this side. On the left, you’ll find two USB-C ports (both of which support external display signals and power delivery), an HDMI port, and a headset jack.
Asus Zenbook 14 (2026) review: Performance
- Fast everyday performance
- Vivid but reflective display
- Good for typing
3DMark: Night Raid: 16,506; Fire Strike: 3,644; Steel Nomad: 224; Solar Bay: 6,135; Solar Bay Unlimited: 6,132; Solar Bay Extreme: 624; Solar Bay Extreme Unlimited: 625
Geekbench 6.5: Multicore: 10,701; Single-core: 2,145
Cinebench R23: Multi Core: 7,403; Cinebench R24: Single Core: 58; Multi Core: 435
Crossmark: Overall: 1,118; Productivity: 1,047; Creativity: 1,188; Responsiveness: 1,132
Passmark Overall: 2,989.3; CPU: 12,886; 2D Graphics: 330.3; 3D Graphics: 1,848.8; Memory: 2,338.2; Disk: 37,339.4
BlackMagicDisk: Read: 3,832MB/s; Write: 2,810MB/s
HandBrake 4K to 1080p: 37.6fps
Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 12 hours and 15 minutes
For everyday tasking, the Zenbook 14 is a solid performer. The Snapdragon X1 chip in my review unit was fast and smooth when conducting basic productivity workloads such as word processing. It also handled multi-tab browsing and 4K streaming with plenty of composure as well.
Sadly, but somewhat expectedly, the Zenbook 14 isn't ideal for a spot of light gaming. It struggled to run Cyberpunk 2077 even on the lowest preset, blighted by rough visuals and debilitating slow downs during chaotic scenes. The A14 I tested previously, equipped with a Snapdragon X2 Elite chip, was able to handle low presets better, although it still wasn’t a flawlessly smooth experience.
Some fan noise is evident when the Zenbook 14 is under stress, but this isn’t too distracting. For such a compact laptop, the Zenbook 14 also does well to keep temperatures from soaring. I only noticed portions above the keyboard and underneath getting hot, while the commonly touchable surfaces, such as the keyboard, only became lukewarm at most.
The 1200p OLED display is crisp and sharp, with plenty of contrast and vividness. It can show reflections a little too readily, especially when deep blacks are displayed. Mostly, though, the high brightness levels do well to keep reflections at bay.
Despite that aforementioned flexing of the keyboard, the Zenbook 14 is still good for typing. It may feel a little harsh due to the lack of dampening, but the keycaps are comfortable and well spaced, while their low profile and short travel make them feel snappy and easy to glide over.
Complementing the keyboard is the super smooth touchpad that allows for easy swipes and gesturing. It’s not very large, but it maximizes its real estate commendably by extending from almost the bottom edge of the unit to the bottom of the space bar, which makes navigation less of a chore than it otherwise would be.
Asus Zenbook 14 (2026) review: Battery life
- Middling longevity compared to rivals
- Zenbook A14 massively outlasts it
- Quick to charge
The battery life of the Zenbook 14 isn’t particularly impressive. When I played a movie on a continuous loop unplugged, its 50Wh battery lasted 12 hours and 15 minutes. While this is quite long, it falls short of quite a few of its rivals.
For context, the A14 has a 70Wh battery, and the difference shows, as that laptop lasted over 28 hours in the same test, one of the best results we’ve seen. And if you’re looking for another enduring 14-inch laptop, the HP OmniBook 7 posted a time of 26 hours. Fortunately, the Zenbook 14 is at least quick to charge, just around two hours to fully top up.
Should I buy the Asus Zenbook 14 (2026)?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Similarly priced rivals are better all-round propositions. | 3 / 5 | 
| Design | The construction is unique, super light, and high in quality, but the flexing keyboard is a small shame. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Performance | Great for everyday tasking, but don't expect more beyond that. It remains remarkably cool and quiet at all times, though. | 4 / 5 | 
| Battery Life | The Zenbook 14 can last a while, but it’s disappointingly short lived compared to rivals. It’s quick to charge, though. | 3.5 / 5 | 
| Final Score | The Zenbook 14 is a capable and highly portable laptop, but when rivals occupying same price point are better all-rounders, they might make more sense. | 3.5 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want something portable
You won’t find many 14-inch laptops more portable than the Zenbook 14, thanks to its compact dimensions and light footprint.
You want a unique design
You won’t find many constructions like this, either: it’s solid with a soft-touch finish and has some interesting colorways to boot.
Don't buy it if…
You want a stable keyboard
While the 14 is great to type with, the keyboard flexing as you do so might irk some users.
You want the best battery life
The Zenbook 14’s battery life isn’t anything special, while the A14’s is.
Asus Zenbook 14 (2026) review: Also consider
Asus Zenbook A14
The A14 is very closely matched to the 14, but it has a much better battery life — the best in class, in fact — and despite having a very similar Ceraluminum construction, it’s ever so slightly lighter (0.98KG as opposed to 1.10KG). It’s similarly priced, too, so might be the better pick of the two. Read our full Asus Zenbook A14 review.
HP OmniBook 7
The OmniBook 7 is a terrific laptop across the board. Its battery life is much longer than Zenbook 14’s, although it can’t quite match the endurance of the aforementioned A14. Its list price is quite steep, but we’ve seen it with significant discounts, bringing it more in line with the Zenbook 14. Read our full HP OmniBook 7 review.
How I tested the Asus Zenbook 14 (2026)
- Tested for a few days
- Used for a variety of tasks and benchmarks
- Extensive laptop reviewing experience
I tested the Zenbook 14 for a few days, during which time I used it for all manner of tasks, from basic productivity and general browsing to 4K streaming and gaming.
I also ran our series of benchmark tests for laptops, designed to assess every aspect of performance. I ran a movie on a loop to test the battery life, too.
I’ve been using laptops for decades, and have reviewed a large number of them, ranging from small budget offerings to large gaming monsters.

He previously worked as a Staff Writer for our business section, TechRadar Pro, where he gained experience with productivity-enhancing hardware, ranging from keyboards to standing desks. His area of expertise lies in computer peripherals and audio hardware, having spent over a decade exploring the murky depths of both PC building and music production. articles.title: OpenAI split a voice model's brain. Then one team deleted 23,000 lines of code.
articles.text:
OpenAI split a voice model’s brain. Then one team deleted 23,000 lines of code.
Building an AI voice agent has always been clunkier than it seems. Most voice agents are really a chain of systems passing a conversation back and forth. What you say gets turned into text so a model can figure out how to respond, then that answer has to be turned back into speech; it’s easy to see why things can get robotic fast. Now, OpenAI is trying to collapse that stack.
On Wednesday, the company launched GPT-Live-1 in its API, bringing the native, full-duplex voice architecture behind ChatGPT voice mode to outside developers for the first time. Instead of making developers manage the entire chain, it wants one model to handle the conversation while the heavier thinking happens elsewhere.
Instead of making developers manage the entire chain, it wants one model to handle the conversation while the heavier thinking happens elsewhere.
Full-duplex voice delegation
GPT-Live-1 operates as the conversational frontline. Because it’s natively full-duplex, it can keep up with a conversation as it happens, including when someone cuts in mid-sentence, without developers coordinating separate systems. But the voice model doesn’t have to do all the work alone.
When a request needs more time or more processing, GPT-Live-1 can hand it off to another model in the background. That could be GPT-6 Astra, a smaller model like Luna, or something from another provider entirely.
Waiting on a bigger model can make a voice agent painfully awkward. Ask a difficult question, and you can end up sitting in silence while the model works through it. GPT-Live-1 can keep the conversation going instead — filling pauses, acknowledging the speaker — then work the answer in once the backend is finished.
OpenAI says GPT-Live-1 performs 30 percentage points better than GPT-Realtime-2.1 on Full Duplex Bench. Paired with GPT-6 Astra at medium reasoning, it also takes the top spot on the 𝜏³-benchmark.
What the handoff looks like
OpenAI exposes delegation through an event-driven interface. The voice session generates a delegation_id, sends context to whatever backend system is handling the heavier work, and gets the result back through an event called session.commentary.append. The voice model folds that result into the ongoing conversation rather than reading a block of text aloud. Developers can still see what the model hears and says and control when it takes a turn — they just don’t have to build the entire conversation out of separate systems. OpenAI’s API docs walk through the full pattern, including a working example with the Codex SDK.
Early customers cut code
One early customer deleted 23,000 lines of code after switching to GPT-Live-1.
Tony Stoyanov, co-founder and CTO of EliseAI, a healthcare company testing the API, said the move shrank his codebase by 80%. His team could spend that time on the patient experience instead — making it easier to book appointments and navigate care.
The language-learning company Speak saw the difference in the conversations themselves. In early tests of its Live Tutor Lessons, GPT-Live-1 was nearly 80% less likely to interrupt someone who had simply paused to think. For someone learning a new language, those extra few seconds can be the difference between getting the answer out and having the AI cut them off.
Yelp is already using GPT-Live-1 in Yelp Host and Hatch. CTO Alex Levy said the company is seeing more calls successfully handled by AI, and callers are speaking in fuller, more natural sentences — a sign, Levy said, that the experience on the other end of the phone feels different. A demo released with the announcement shows exactly why, when a restaurant reservation kept moving even with background noise, and people spoke over one another.
Pricing the voice layer
GPT-Live-1 costs $0.05 per minute, or about $3 an hour. Then there’s whatever developers choose to run behind it. If GPT-Live-1 hands a request to GPT-6 Astra, the developer pays for that call too. The more often an agent reaches for a reasoning model, the faster the bill climbs.
OpenAI has been cutting API prices as competition from Anthropic, Google, and Chinese labs heats up, but frontier reasoning still isn’t free.
The more often an agent reaches for a reasoning model, the faster the bill climbs.
The tradeoff is that developers can now be selective about where they spend that money. Something simple, like scheduling an appointment, could go to Luna. A harder question, like one that actually needs multi-step reasoning or tool calls, could go to Astra. OpenAI has already shown how Astra’s adjustable reasoning settings let developers dial cost up or down per call, and GPT-Live-1 gives them a place to apply that same logic to voice.
Platform control tradeoffs
With the older cascaded approach, teams can choose a different provider for each part of the voice stack and swap pieces out when they want. GPT-Live-1 takes over more of the conversation, which also means handing more of it to OpenAI.
The bet is that developers will give up some of that control if it means voice agents can finally keep up with the people talking to them.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday record chez Microsoft, 974 failles corrigées dans une course contre la montre accélérée par l’IA
articles.text:
Microsoft n’a jamais corrigé autant de vulnérabilités en un seul Patch Tuesday. Derrière ce volume hors norme, des enjeux de sécurité toujours plus pressants, alors que l’IA accélère la course entre découverte et exploitation des failles.
Les Patch Tuesday se suivent et prennent désormais des proportions inédites. Après un record en juillet et un mois d’août particulièrement chargé, celui de septembre vient une fois encore pulvériser les compteurs. Au total, Microsoft confirme avoir corrigé 974 failles dans l’ensemble de ses produits, parmi lesquelles 723 concernent la seule famille Windows. Une mise à jour à installer au plus vite, alors que deux vulnérabilités sont déjà exploitées dans des attaques et que l’IA compresse les délais des deux côtés : Microsoft débusque les failles plus vite, tout comme les attaquants, qui peuvent alors les exploiter plus rapidement.
La solution tout-en-un pour protéger votre entreprise
Votre petite entreprise a de grandes ambitions. Protégez-là contre les pirates. Et développez sereinement votre activité !
Deux failles d'élévation de privilèges déjà exploitées et peu contraignantes à déclencher
Dans le détail, CVE-2026-81963 (CVSS 7,8) touche la pile Windows Update sur Windows 11 23H2, 24H2, 25H2 et 26H1, ainsi que Windows Server 2025. Il faut savoir qu’au moment d’installer les mises à jour, Windows Update intervient sur des fichiers système avec des privilèges élevés. La faille permet ici à un attaquant ayant déjà obtenu un accès local au PC de détourner l’accès à ces fichiers vers une autre cible, puis de profiter de ces privilèges élevés pour décrocher les droits SYSTEM sur la machine.
La seconde zero-day, CVE-2026-85880 (CVSS 7,8), touche Windows ALPC, le système de communication utilisé par les processus locaux pour échanger des données entre eux. Un dépassement de tampon dans la mémoire peut permettre à du code exécuté avec de faibles privilèges dans un AppContainer, un environnement isolé de Windows, de sortir de cette sandbox et d’obtenir, là encore, les droits SYSTEM sur la machine. Cette vulnérabilité concerne Windows 10 21H2 et 22H2, ainsi que Windows Server 2012 à 2022.
Ces failles ne permettent donc pas, à elles seules, de compromettre un ordinateur à distance, mais elles peuvent transformer un premier accès limité en contrôle presque total de la machine. Microsoft précise en revanche que leur exploitation ne requiert ni condition particulière ni intervention de la victime, d’où l’importance de ne pas tarder à appliquer les correctifs correspondants.
Avec l’IA, le temps laissé pour appliquer les patchs fond à vue d’œil
Si Microsoft en arrive aujourd’hui à corriger près de mille failles en un mois, ce n’est pas tant parce que ses produits et services se seraient soudainement dégradés, mais parce qu’elle en repère davantage, et beaucoup plus vite. L’entreprise avait prévenu au printemps que ses bulletins de sécurité allaient gonfler à mesure que les signalements augmenteraient et que ses propres outils de recherche assistés par IA gagneraient en efficacité.
Redmond s’appuie notamment sur MDASH, son système de découverte et de correction des vulnérabilités piloté par plusieurs agents IA. En mai, il avait déjà permis d’identifier 16 failles dans des composants réseau et d’authentification de Windows, dont quatre vulnérabilités critiques permettant l’exécution de code à distance. Depuis, les Patch Tuesday enchaînent les mois hors norme, jusqu’à battre deux fois leur record en l’espace de trois mois.
Mais cette capacité à traquer les failles plus vite ne profite pas qu’à Microsoft. L’IA aide aussi les attaquants à analyser plus rapidement les vulnérabilités divulguées, à en comprendre le fonctionnement et à passer plus vite à leur exploitation.
Une course contre la montre qui a conduit Microsoft à durcir ses recommandations pour les parcs administrés dès cet été. L’entreprise conseille désormais de limiter à moins de trois jours l’attente précédant le déploiement des mises à jour qualité, de fixer leur délai d’installation à un jour grand maximum et de plafonner la période de grâce à deux jours, au terme de laquelle le redémarrage des machines devrait être imposé.

articles.title: Überraschend schnell: Warum der Mond in nur 5 Stunden entstanden sein könnte
articles.text:
Überraschend schnell: Warum der Mond in nur 5 Stunden entstanden sein könnte
Seit Jahrzehnten gilt die sogenannte Giant-Impact-Hypothese als plausibelste Erklärung für unseren Trabanten. Analysen von alten Apollo-Gesteinsproben stützen die Annahme, dass die junge Erde vor rund 4,5 Milliarden Jahren mit dem Protoplaneten Theia kollidierte. Offen blieb jedoch stets die Frage, wie schnell sich der Mond aus den Trümmern formte. Klassische Modelle gehen von einer rotierenden Trümmerscheibe aus, aus der der Himmelskörper über Monate oder gar Jahre heranwuchs.
Neuere Berechnungen deuteten zwar bereits an, dass dieser Prozess deutlich rasanter abgelaufen sein könnte. Eine aktuelle Untersuchung rückt nun jedoch ein bisher übersehenes Detail in den Fokus, das die Mondentstehung in einem gänzlich neuen Licht erscheinen lässt, nämlich die Temperatur und die daraus resultierende geologische Materialfestigkeit der kollidierenden Körper.
Weiches Material formt einen schnellen Begleiter
Das Team um die Planetenforscherin Adeene Denton vom US-amerikanischen Southwest Research Institute in Boulder nutzte für seine Untersuchung die sogenannte Smoothed-Particle-Hydrodynamics-Methode (SPH). Wie die in The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichte Arbeit detailliert darlegt, simulierten die Wissenschaftler:innen den Einschlag mit bis zu einer Million Datenpartikeln. Bei diesem gitterlosen Verfahren wird die kosmische Materie durch unzählige einzelne Punkte repräsentiert, deren physikalische Zustände das System kontinuierlich berechnet.
Die entscheidende Neuerung dieser digitalen Architektur war der Einbezug der geologischen Festigkeit. Bisherige Berechnungen behandelten die kollidierenden Körper zumeist als rein fluide Massen. Das Forschungsteam berücksichtigte nun jedoch präzise, wie die jeweilige Temperatur die Widerstandskraft des Gesteins verändert. Heißere Protoplaneten reagieren bei einer Kollision weicher und verformbarer, während kühlere Körper wesentlich spröder sind. Genau dieser thermische Zustand entschied im virtuellen Modell über das finale Schicksal von Theia.
Kühlere Ausgangsbedingungen lieferten in der Simulation exakt das, was auch alte Modelle zeigten, nämlich eine weiträumige Trümmerscheibe, die die frühe Erde umgab. Trafen hingegen thermisch passende, heißere Körper aufeinander, zerschellte Theia nicht vollständig. Ein gewaltiges Teilstück spaltete sich ab und blieb ausreichend gravitativ gebunden. Im Ergebnis formte sich in nur etwa fünf Stunden ein intakter, mondgroßer Trabant in einer erdnahen Umlaufbahn.
Komplexe Gezeitenkräfte retten den jungen Mond
Möglich wurde dieser Schnellstart durch komplexe Gezeitenkräfte, die das Forschungsteam anschaulich als „walking the dog“ bezeichnet. Der Vorgang ist hochdynamisch. Ein inneres, massereicheres Fragment Theias stürzt auf die Erde und überträgt dabei seinen Drehimpuls auf das äußere Teilstück. Die Erde hält dieses verbliebene Fragment durch die gravitativen Wechselwirkungen quasi an einer unsichtbaren Leine und manövriert es so auf eine stabile Bahn, die es vor der endgültigen Zerstörung bewahrt.
Wer nun allerdings an einen hell leuchtenden, fertigen Trabanten am irdischen Nachthimmel denkt, zieht den falschen Schluss. Die rasante Fünf-Stunden-Bildung lieferte, wenn überhaupt, lediglich den physikalischen Grundkörper. Dieser frisch geschmiedete Satellit wäre glühend heiß und komplett von einem tiefen Magmaozean bedeckt gewesen. Sein langsames Erstarren und die weitere geologische Entwicklung bis zu dem Himmelskörper, den wir heute kennen, hätten im Anschluss noch viele Millionen Jahre in Anspruch genommen.
Spurensuche bei fernen Exoplaneten
Da Protoplaneten über die Jahrmillionen kontinuierlich auskühlen, lassen sich aus der in der Simulation benötigten Temperaturstruktur theoretisch Rückschlüsse auf den exakten Zeitpunkt des historischen Einschlags ziehen. Einen verbindlichen Zeitstempel liefert die aktuelle Studie aber noch nicht. Vielmehr öffnet sie den Blick für andere gewaltige Ereignisse in unserem Sonnensystem. So könnten ähnliche Berechnungen künftig helfen, die Entstehung des Saturnmondes Titan oder die ungewöhnliche Achsneigung des Jupitermondes Ganymed besser zu verstehen.
Die Erkenntnisse strahlen zudem direkt auf die Suche nach fernen Exomonden ab, wie Phys.org einordnet. Bislang halten Astronom:innen bei Exoplaneten oft gezielt nach ausgedehnten Trümmerwolken Ausschau, um frische planetare Kollisionen nachzuweisen. Entstehen massereiche Monde jedoch direkt als intakte Körper, verschwinden diese verräterischen Spuren im All deutlich schneller als bisher angenommen.
Ein direkter Nachweis ferner Trabanten wird durch diese Erkenntnis zwar nicht automatisch leichter, aber die Suchparameter der Astronomie könnten sich nachhaltig verschieben. Ob die Erde ihren ständigen Begleiter tatsächlich auf diesem extrem schnellen Weg bekam, bleibt bis auf Weiteres ein faszinierendes physikalisches Gedankenmodell. Letztlich müssen künftige Analysen von echtem, durch kommende Raumfahrtmissionen gesammeltem Mondgestein zeigen, welches Entstehungsszenario die chemische Realität unseres Trabanten am verlässlichsten abbildet.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 10, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (September 10, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, September 10, 2026.
From AllSecureX’s pre-seed backing for quantum-resilient cyber defence to Inbound Aerospace’s India-Australia space-testing MoU and Swiggy’s Snowflake-powered data overhaul, to new fintech launches at Global Fintech Fest, YourStory brings you today's headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Funding news
AllSecureX raises undisclosed pre-seed from Finvolve, India Accelerator
Finvolve, along with India Accelerator, has invested an undisclosed amount in AllSecureX, an Indian DeepTech and cybersecurity startup. The company said the pre-seed funding will support Phase 2 product development, controlled defence and space pilots, IP creation, hiring across engineering and business roles, and readiness for iDEX and Indian Army opportunities.
Founded in 2025 by Himanshu Vohra, AllSecureX is building a hardware-independent, software-defined platform to discover cryptographic assets, quantify long-term quantum risk and orchestrate transitions to post-quantum cryptography in classified and air-gapped environments.
According to the company, Phase 1 of its QERA platform has run 2,781 assessments across 229 validation environments; it has eight pilot-interest and validation requests, and has filed five patents. The next phase, Quantum Discovery, is being aligned with NIST post-quantum standards and DRDO requirements.
Other news
Inbound Aerospace, Space Angel sign 5-year spacecraft testing MoU
Inbound Aerospace said it has signed a five-year memorandum of understanding with Australia’s Space Angel Group to explore collaboration across flight and drop testing, high-altitude and near-space trials, recovery operations, spaceport infrastructure and mission planning. Effective September 2026, the MoU sets a three-year framework to assess how Space Angel’s infrastructure can support testing and demonstration of Inbound’s re-entry and lifting-body systems, with scope for joint tech development, pilots and market expansion in India and Australia.
The Chennai-based, IIT Madras-incubated startup said it is developing an autonomous, unmanned, recoverable re-entry spacecraft for low-Earth-orbit missions spanning microgravity research, in-orbit tech demonstrations, in-space manufacturing and payload return, alongside precision-landing capabilities relevant to defence and disaster response. Inbound Aerospace is led by co-founders Dr Aravind I B, Vishal Reddy and Capt Abhijit Bhutey (Retd.).
Swiggy adopts Snowflake to speed data decisions and access
Snowflake announced that Swiggy is using its AI Data Cloud as a unified data foundation across food delivery, Instamart and Dineout. According to Snowflake, Swiggy’s slowest data workflows improved by 90 to 96%, heavy queries dropped from two hours to 15 minutes, and data processing moved from six hours to near real time.
The companies said employees now have governed self-service access with role-based controls, column masking and row-level security, while operational teams monitor service quality metrics in real time. “At Swiggy, data is valuable only when it reaches the person who can act on it,” said Madhusudhan Rao, Chief Technology Officer, Swiggy.
Google unveils five India sustainability and clean energy initiatives
Google announced five India-focused sustainability initiatives spanning rooftop solar intelligence, clean power procurement, climate-smart agriculture and research. The company said Solar API insights now cover over 300 million Indian rooftops; it has signed a new 150 MW solar agreement in Rajasthan with ReNew Power; and it is partnering with Mitti Labs on a methane- and water-reduction project for smallholder rice farmers in Telangana.
Google said Solar API, part of Earth AI, helps local platforms such as Solar Ladder and OpenSolar automate assessments and proposals. The ReNew deal will provide environmental attributes to address value-chain electricity emissions, while the Mitti Labs project aims to mitigate nearly three million tonnes of CO2e on a GWP20 basis with satellite-enabled verification. The Google Center for Climate Technology is also adding new focus areas on water stewardship and waste and circularity.
News from Global Fintech Fest
CCAvenue integrates Amazon Pay Balance for faster checkouts
AvenuesAI said its payment gateway CCAvenue has integrated Amazon Pay Balance, enabling merchants to offer customers a familiar stored-balance option at checkout. Unveiled at Global Fintech Fest 2026, the integration aims to improve payment success rates and reduce checkout abandonment across CCAvenue’s merchant network.
The companies said Amazon Pay Balance has over 70 million customers and that deep-link integration supports secure transactions and higher conversions. “Our goal is to make digital transactions as intuitive, secure, and rewarding as possible,” said Neha Gupta Mahatame, Director, Stored Value and Gifting, Amazon Pay.
Xflow, HSBC launch India collections for global businesses
Xflow announced a partnership with HSBC to let global businesses collect payments from Indian customers via UPI, net banking and cards without setting up a local entity. The company said the solution converts cross-border payments into local transactions to boost conversion, with UPI and cards delivering a 95%+ success rate.
Xflow said settlement is available in major currencies and that the product targets categories such as physical goods, SaaS, AI platforms, travel and edtech. The company holds final authorisation under the RBI’s Payment Aggregator Cross Border framework for exports and imports, and as a Payment Aggregator Online, has in-principle IFSCA approval to operate as a Payment Service Provider at GIFT City, and is registered in Canada as an MSB.
Mahindra Finance, Sarvam expand voice AI across operations
Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services said it has expanded its voice AI partnership with Sarvam, extending agents across sales, collections and employee engagement. Announced at GFF 2026, the companies said voice agents built by Mahindra AI on Sarvam’s platform operate in 12 Indian languages and have completed over one crore calls.
Use cases include relationship checks and cross-sell in sales, pre-due reminders through write-off-stage outreach in collections, and field feedback for employee engagement, with custom AI pipelines recording and analysing calls that feed downstream systems.
“Voice AI has allowed us to extend that closeness at scale,” said Raul Rebello, Managing Director and CEO, Mahindra Finance.
HyperVerge launches AI underwriting suite for MSME loans
HyperVerge launched an AI agents suite for business loan underwriting, designed to reduce manual work on complex MSME files to under an hour while keeping decisions with credit managers. Announced at GFF 2026, the company said pilots with about 10 mid-size lenders cut financial assessment time from two to three hours to five minutes, and turned four-hour appraisal memos around in under 10 minutes.
The suite includes agents for financial data collection and checks, a video personal discussion assistant available in 10 to 12 languages, and background due diligence that links recommendations to source documents and timestamps. Pricing is usage-based. “Our AI agents automate that assembly work, pulling documents, compiling data, and running credit parameters,” said Kedar Kulkarni, CEO and Co-founder, HyperVerge.
Razorpay showcases Vulcan AI payments model to Prime Minister
Razorpay presented Vulcan, which the company described as India’s first AI payments foundation model, to Prime Minister Narendra Modi at GFF 2026 in Mumbai. The company said Vulcan is trained on nearly three trillion data points across four billion payments to improve success rates, strengthen fraud detection and streamline checkout.
Razorpay said businesses including Blinkit, Bachatt and redBus are seeing an 8 to 10% improvement in payment success rates and an eightfold increase in international card fraud detection. The company added that Vulcan is built to make online transactions faster, safer and smarter for merchants and customers.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Un ladrón huyó por los tejados de un pueblo de Toledo. Cuando la Guardia Civil lo acorraló, sacó un bastón-estoque
articles.text:
Ocurrió el 30 de agosto, aunque la Guardia Civil no lo hizo público hasta el 9 de septiembre. La central de alarmas avisó de un robo en curso en una vivienda de Corral de Almaguer (Toledo). Una patrulla de la Guardia Civil, reforzada por agentes de la Policía Local, llegó en minutos y sorprendió a uno de los presuntos ladrones saltando de tejado en tejado y colándose por los patios de las casas colindantes, en una huida que recorrió buena parte del casco antiguo del pueblo. Parece un noir, con sombras corriendo sobre la loza roja en plena noche.
Pero lo mejor llega al final. La persecución terminó en una zona sin salida. Acorralado, el joven sacó de entre la ropa un bastón-estoque e intentó atacar a los agentes. La pieza, especialmente ornamentada, tenía más pinta de atrezo de Arsène Lupin o del profesor Moriarty que de arma de pueblo. Los agentes lo redujeron por la fuerza. Y en el forcejeo resultaron heridos dos guardias civiles y un policía local. Dentro de la vivienda y en los alrededores, los agentes localizaron además distintos efectos ya reunidos, listos para sacarlos del domicilio.
Qué es exactamente un bastón-estoque: no es un cuchillo ni una navaja, es un bastón corriente que esconde una hoja fina en su interior, oculta bajo el puño o el regatón, y pensado precisamente para pasar desapercibido. El objeto tiene siglos de historia como accesorio de caballero: en el siglo XIX era casi de etiqueta entre la burguesía europea, un complemento elegante con truco incluido. Pero condenable.
El Reglamento de Armas lo cataloga de forma expresa como arma prohibida en su artículo 4, en la misma lista que las navajas automáticas, los puños americanos o las armas de fuego camufladas bajo la apariencia de otro objeto. La ley no distingue aquí por peligrosidad bruta, sino por disimulo: lo prohibido no es solo el filo, es esconderlo a plena vista dentro de un objeto tan inocente como un bastón de paseo.
Los cargos. Los investigadores identificaron y detuvieron después al segundo implicado en el robo, en una operación separada. Los dos detenidos tienen 19 y 22 años, y a ambos se les acusa de un delito de robo con fuerza. Al que sacó el bastón-estoque se le suman además dos cargos más graves: atentado contra agentes de la autoridad y desobediencia grave. Ningún herido de gravedad y un objeto insólito que terminará archivado como prueba.
El Código Penal castiga el atentado contra un agente con entre 6 meses y 3 años de cárcel, una horquilla que sube hasta los cuatro años cuando, como aquí, el agresor emplea un arma en la acometida. Junto con las diligencias, los dos pasaron a disposición del Tribunal de Instancia número 2 de Quintanar de la Orden. La Guardia Civil da la operación por cerrada y no prevé nuevas detenciones.
En Corral de Almaguer. El pueblo tiene algo más de 5.000 habitantes y se asienta a ambos lados del río Riánsares, rodeado de viñedos de la Denominación de Origen La Mancha, en plena comarca toledana del mismo nombre. Su origen se remonta, según los registros locales, hasta el Neolítico, aunque el pueblo que hoy se visita creció durante la Edad Media entre hidalgos y comunidades musulmanas.
Queda a poco más de 100 kilómetros de la capital provincial, y a poco más de una hora de Madrid. Pertenece al partido judicial de Quintanar, el mismo que ahora instruye el caso. En su casco histórico sobresale la iglesia de la Asunción, del siglo XVI y estilo gótico plateresco. Don Íñigo López Dávalos, comendador de Corral de Almaguer en el siglo XV, tuvo un hijo, Alfonso de Ávalos, marqués del Vasto, al que Tiziano retrató dos veces; una de esas obras cuelga hoy en el Museo del Prado. Y otro corraleño, Bartolomé Romero, cruzó el Atlántico en 1598 con la expedición fundacional de Nuevo México y dio origen a una de las familias más influyentes de aquella colonia.
Corral de Almaguer suele aparecer en la prensa por otro motivo: es la localidad natal de la periodista Sara Carbonero. Y haciendo algo de periodismo: la historiografía local sostiene que Miguel de Cervantes cruzó su camino con corraleños en cada tramo turbio de su biografía: Álvaro de Sande, comendador de Corral de Almaguer y amigo de su padre, comandaba el Tercio de Nápoles en el que se alistó tras huir de España en 1569, condenado en rebeldía a perder una mano.
Y espera, que no hemos terminado: durante su cautiverio en Argel entabló amistad con otro corraleño, Alonso Hernández, al que ayudó a escapar; y años después, un vecino de la villa, Francisco Suárez Gasco, avaló su trabajo como recaudador de impuestos y acabó cargándole el muerto cuando el dinero desapareció, lo que le costó la cárcel donde, se cree, empezó a escribir el Quijote. Ni en su entierro faltó un corraleño: el escribano que le alquilaba el piso en Madrid ejerció de testigo.

articles.title: Un naufragio, tres días y recursos limitados: el juego gratuito de supervivencia disponible en Steam
articles.text:
Un naufragio, tres días y recursos limitados definen 30 Days On Ship: Castaway – The First Days, un juego gratuito de supervivencia disponible en Steam para PC. La propuesta coloca al jugador entre los restos de un buque portacontenedores encallado contra una costa rocosa, donde cada objeto puede servir para mantenerse con vida y descubrir qué ocurrió antes del desastre que lo cambió todo.
Cómo es el nuevo juego gratuito de Steam
El título presenta a un náufrago que debe sobrevivir durante tres días después de un accidente marítimo. Su escenario no es una isla convencional, sino un enorme carguero que terminó varado frente a una costa. Esa elección convierte las bodegas, cubiertas y restos de la embarcación en zonas de búsqueda, aunque también obliga a calcular riesgos antes de alejarse de los recursos encontrados.
PUBLICIDAD
El tiempo limitado marca el ritmo de la partida. No basta con hallar materiales: el jugador necesita decidir qué conservar, qué utilizar y cuándo avanzar. La supervivencia depende de aprovechar objetos de formas poco habituales, una mecánica que busca dar valor a herramientas aparentemente menores. Cada recorrido puede aportar una solución, pero también consumir tiempo y exponer al personaje a peligros del barco.
Por ese planteamiento, 30 Days On Ship: Castaway – The First Days se acerca más a una aventura de exploración y gestión que a un juego centrado solo en acción. El interés está en examinar espacios, reunir elementos y comprender la situación del protagonista. El entorno ofrece materiales útiles, pero exige atención constante, ya que una decisión calculada puede reducir las alternativas para continuar.
PUBLICIDAD
La propuesta presenta una experiencia breve, enfocada en los primeros momentos posteriores al accidente. El jugador debe interpretar el entorno y encontrar formas de utilizar los recursos disponibles. La tensión surge de la necesidad de actuar con lo que está al alcance, sin depender de grandes inventarios ni de herramientas preparadas antes de comenzar la aventura.
Cómo descargar el juego gratis desde Steam
Para incorporarlo a la biblioteca, el proceso parte de una cuenta activa en Steam. El usuario debe abrir la aplicación de PC o la tienda web, escribir el nombre completo del juego en la barra de búsqueda y comprobar que aparece con precio cero. Después debe pulsar Obtener, Añadir a la biblioteca o Jugar, según la opción disponible, y confirmar incorporación al perfil.
PUBLICIDAD
Una vez añadido, el título queda asociado con la cuenta y puede instalarse cuando el jugador disponga de espacio en el ordenador. Esa posibilidad permite reclamarlo primero y descargarlo después, sin necesidad de llenar el disco de inmediato. También conviene consultar la ficha antes de instalarlo, porque allí figuran requisitos técnicos, idiomas compatibles, controles disponibles y información que el estudio publique sobre actualizaciones.
Steam usa los juegos gratuitos para ampliar su catálogo
Steam combina lanzamientos comerciales con juegos gratuitos, demostraciones y periodos de prueba que sirven a los estudios para conseguir visibilidad. Para los equipos independientes, ofrecer una experiencia sin costo puede acercar un proyecto a jugadores que no lo habrían encontrado entre miles de novedades. Para el público, estas propuestas permiten probar géneros distintos y decidir después si quiere seguir futuras entregas o desarrollos.
PUBLICIDAD
El acceso digital aporta actualizaciones automáticas y una biblioteca que puede consultarse desde diferentes equipos vinculados a la misma cuenta. A la vez, conviene recordar que los juegos obtenidos en estas plataformas corresponden a licencias de uso sujetas a sus políticas. Esa condición no cambia que las promociones y los títulos sin coste amplíen las alternativas de quienes juegan en ordenador cada día.
30 Days On Ship: Castaway – The First Days propone una escala reducida frente a otros juegos de supervivencia, pero utiliza el naufragio para convertir recursos comunes en decisiones relevantes. La oferta gratuita facilita conocer una experiencia centrada en la observación y la administración. En un catálogo extenso como Steam, localizar propuestas así depende de revisar novedades con atención, no solo los lanzamientos visibles.

articles.title: Les Redmi Note 17 sont là avec des batteries XXL jamais vues en France
articles.text:
Xiaomi annonce ses tout nouveaux Redmi Note. Déjà ? Oui, alors que les Redmi Note 15 datent du mois de janvier 2026, voici que déboulent déjà leurs héritiers. Et tant qu’à faire, ils ont eux aussi sauté le 16 pour arriver directement sur le 17, pour s’aligner sur les Xiaomi 17 et l’iPhone 17 (malgré l’arrivée très prochaine de l’iPhone 18 Pro).
2026, pas une année comme les autres pour les Redmi
Comme à son habitude, la gamme est très segmentée, avec une montée progressive en qualité pour s’étaler du très entrée de gamme jusqu’au milieu de gamme. Avant de plonger dans les fiches techniques, il nous faut nous arrêter sur un point : cette année 2026, marquée pas l’augmentation des prix des composants à cause de la RAMpocalypse, n’aura épargné personne et pas même Xiaomi.
Certains modèles de Redmi Note sont moins bien équipés, par certains aspects, que leurs prédécesseurs, avec notamment la disparition en entrée de gamme d’un module ultra grand-angle. Heureusement Xiaomi se rattrape sur les capacités de batterie (merci le Silicum Carbone).
Toute la gamme profitera de 4 ans de mises à jour Android et 6 ans de mises à jour de sécurité.
Les Redmi 17 Pro : le cœur de gamme
On commence par le modèle le plus équilibré de la gamme, le Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G. Comme le laisse penser la mention Pro, il ne s’agit pas de l’entrée de gamme, mais plutôt du dernier arrêt avant le modèle le plus cher de tous les Redmi cette année.
Pour ce prix, vous aurez le droit à un large écran de 6,83 pouces avec une résolution de 447 PPP, le tout sur une dalle OLED 120 Hz capable de monter, d’après le constructeur, jusqu’à 3500 nits.
Concernant la configuration photo, le Redmi Note 17 Pro propose un double module photo au dos, avec un grand angle de 50 Mpx et un ultra grand-angle de 8 Mpx. Le module selfie monte à 16 Mpx.
On l’a dit, cette année, Xiaomi mise gros sur l’autonomie pour se distinguer. Le 17 Pro en est la preuve, puisqu’il intègre 8340 mAh de batterie, une capacité encore jamais vue sur un appareil en France. D’après la marque, le téléphone devrait tenir 3 jours consécutifs. Nous ne manquerons pas de vérifier cela lors de notre test complet. Pour alimenter l’animal, la marque propose une charge propriétaire jusqu’à 67W en filaire et 22,5 W de charge inversée.
Quelques concessions techniques au programme
Pour terminer le tour du propriétaire, notons que le Redmi Note ne devrait pas, comme à son habitude, faire exploser les records de puissance. Il possède en effet une puce relativement modeste, un Snapdragon 6s Gen 4, aidé par 6 à 8 Go de RAM LPDDR4X, une version un peu moins véloce que l’actuelle LPDDR5x, ainsi qu’un stockage UFS 2.2, lui aussi un peu dépassé face à la norme UFS 3 voire 4 que l’on retrouve sur des modèles plus chers. Le modem est du même tonneau, puisqu’il supporte du WiFi 5, un standard un peu en retard sur les plus récents WiFi 6 et 7.
Un mot sur le design : le téléphone est étanche (IP 68), relativement épais (8,6 mm) et pas le plus léger du marché (215g). Il intègre des tranches plates en plastique et du Gorilla Glass Victus 2 pour se protéger des rayures.
Avant de passer au modèle suivant, terminons par préciser que s’il existe bien un modèle Pro 4G, celui-ci ne sera pas disponible en France pour la première fois.
Redmi Note 17 Pro Max : toute ressemblance avec une marque dotée d’une pomme est fortuite
Le sommet de la gamme s’appellera Redmi Note 17… Pro Max. Exit le Pro Plus donc, et bienvenue à un nom très original !
Blague à part, celui-ci propose pas mal d’améliorations par rapport au modèle précédent, à commencer par une batterie encore plus grande. Elle monte alors à 9210 mAh ! Il s’agit à notre connaissance de la plus grosse batterie disponible sur le marché en France. Elle profite en outre d’une charge de 100W en filaire.
Pour justifier sa montée en gamme, Xiaomi a également mis une puce un peu plus véloce, le Snapdragon 6 Gen 5. En outre, la marque opte pour de la RAM et du stockage de meilleure qualité, passant à la génération LPDDR5x et UFS 4.0. Il en va de même pour les technologies de réseaux sans fil, avec l’introduction du Bluetooth 6.0 et du WiFi 6. Le smartphone profitera également de quelques fonctionnalités IA en plus, puisqu’il fait partie des smartphones siglés Xiaomi HyperAI.
Au delà des différences techniques pures, le smartphone profite d’un cadre en métal, ainsi que des coins incurvés côté écran pour une prise en main un peu plus sympa.
Redmi Note 17 : un entrée de gamme plus grand
Terminons par les modèles les moins chers, les Redmi Note 17 4G et 5G. Note. Contrairement à d’autres années, ils sont ce coup-ci relativement proche en termes de fiche technique. La principale différence entre les deux modèles, du passage 4G/5G, réside dans les entrailles du téléphone. En effet, le Redmi Note 17 4G devrait être assez modeste sur les performances, avec non seulement une puce assez ancienne, le Snapdragon 6s Gen 2, mais aussi seulement 4 Go de RAM. La version 5G monte à 6 Go avec une puce un peu plus véloce, le Snapdragon 4 Gen 4.
Les deux smartphones opèrent des concessions assez importantes par rapport au modèle Pro, et même par rapport à leurs prédécesseurs, puisque l’on a cette année seulement un capteur photo au dos (!) de 50 Mpx.
Côté charge et batterie, il en va de même avec une batterie certes plus petite, mais toujours très convenable si on la compare au reste du marché, puisqu’elle monte à 7700 mAh, pour une charge à 45W. Les smartphones troquent également le verre Corning Victus 2 pour du Gorilla Glass 7i un peu moins résistant.
Xiaomi souhaite communiquer sur les prix de ces produits dans un second temps. Nous vous les transmettrons alors.

articles.title: In a bizarre twist, robots protest in Poland to warn that AI and automation could take human jobs
articles.text:
WTF?! In an ironic turn of events, humanoid and quadrupedal robots in Poland protested outside of the country's digital affairs ministry. The machines demanded increased regulation of AI and automation to protect human jobs from being replaced. But this wasn't some kind of Futurama-like scenario where the robots had decided to stick up for us meat sacks.
The protest, which saw around 30 robots "chanting" slogans, holding signs, and marching in circles, was organized by Democratism. The group aims to launch a public debate on how rapid AI and advancements in robotization impact the human labor market, according to its website.
"We want regulations, we want rules, we want law" were some of the chants played through loudspeakers. "Don't wait, regulate, protect jobs."
Organizer Grzegorz Kuliś said, "We particularly want to address the issue of the potential replacement of people both by humanoid robots and by artificial intelligence in cognitive work."
 – Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) September 7, 2026
The use of the robots was meant to illustrate that the threat of machines and AI taking jobs is no longer theoretical. With the robots' existing capabilities on show, it was hoped that the display would make people pay attention and spark a debate.
"If we don't react now, we may soon have a problem," Kuliś said.
The word "protesting" is doing a lot of heavy lifting here. The video shows the machines being manually placed, the chanting was reportedly pre-loaded, and there isn't a whole lot of movement going on – it doesn't look like the riot police were on standby.
That's not to say the threat isn't real. There have been numerous stories about humanoid robots moving into jobs traditionally occupied by people who inconveniently require wages, breaks, and the occasional day off.
Amazon has long been using robots in its warehouses, while BMW announced plans to put Figure's humanoids to work in its factories. Hyundai's proposed deployment prompted its union to warn of a "huge employment shock."
The companies tend to insist the machines will help workers, not replace them – a line that's becoming very familiar. Arm's CEO was rather less reassuring, predicting that AI-powered robots would replace most factory workers within five to ten years.
That's not to mention the AI-specific job losses that are happening across the globe, either. US tech firms in particular have laid off tens of thousands of people in recent times as they focus on automation and paying for AI infrastructure.
"We are constantly debating the impact of migrants on our society, whilst the vast majority of 'migrants' will arrive either via undersea cables across the Atlantic in the form of AI agents, or as humanoid robots in shipping containers from China," Kuliś warned.

articles.title: Agora é oficial: Google passa a liberar um novo Chrome a cada duas semanas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Agora é oficial: Google passa a liberar um novo Chrome a cada duas semanas
Mudança começou com Google Chrome 153. Medida visa diminuir exposição do navegador a vulnerabilidades.
A partir deste mês de setembro, o Google passa a liberar uma versão final do Chrome a cada duas semanas. Até então, cada nova versão era lançada em ciclos de quatro semanas. A nova abordagem tem um objetivo importante: aumentar a segurança do navegador.
O Google anunciou o ciclo quinzenal de atualizações do Chrome em março deste ano. Com esse ritmo, atualizações de segurança passam a ser implementadas mais rapidamente, de modo que o browser fique menos tempo exposto a vulnerabilidades. A própria companhia explica:
Reduzir a janela entre o lançamento de uma correção na base de código pública e a entrega aos usuários finais mantém a lacuna de patch “N-day” [intervalo entre a divulgação de uma vulnerabilidade e a sua correção] o menor possível, ajudando a nos proteger contra ameaças em rápida evolução.
Ben Mason e Deepak Ravichandran, do Google
O Google estreou a nova abordagem com o Chrome 153, versão liberada oficialmente em 8 de setembro. A próxima versão, a 154, será lançada em 22 de setembro. Esse ciclo de atualização quinzenal será mantido nos meses subsequentes, tanto nas versões móveis (iOS e Android) quanto no desktop.
Para organizações, o Google continua oferecendo o Chrome via canal “Extended Stable”. Nele, grandes conjuntos de atualizações são liberados em ciclos de oito semanas para que a organização tenha tempo de testar e implementar as novas versões. Porém, as correções mais importantes são liberadas semanalmente.
Um detalhe interessante é que o novo ciclo de atualizações pode, eventualmente, acelerar a chegada de novas funcionalidades ao navegador. Mas o foco da mudança está mesmo no aspecto da segurança: em tempos em que a IA pode e é usada para identificação ou exploração de vulnerabilidades, a mitigação precisa ser tão ou mais rápida.
Vale lembrar que o Google ativou outra proteção importante no browser recentemente: um mecanismo que “blinda” o Chrome contra roubo de contas.

articles.title: Physicist does the math on Star Trek’s “Picard maneuver”
articles.text:
It turns out Jean-Luc Picard was an even better starship helmsman than the writers knew. A physicist has gone through the details of a warp-speed trick from the first season of Star Trek: The Next Generation and found a subtlety the show missed. But instead of a plot hole, the detail he found actually makes the maneuver more impressive… as well as a great opportunity to teach about a lesser-known feature of the theory of relativity.
Níckolas de Aguiar Alves, a physicist at the Federal University of ABC in Brazil, first watched Next Generation as a master’s student. When he got to the episode “The Battle” in the show’s first season, the plot reminded him of his relativity coursework.
In “The Battle,” a Ferengi leader reminds Picard of a battle he fought years ago as captain of a ship called the Stargazer. Under fire from a mysterious attacker, Picard’s ship’s shields were down. He had to get closer without taking a hit, so he made a gamble. Picard ordered the Stargazer to charge the enemy ship at warp speed (meaning faster than light), then stop abruptly and fire. By going faster than light, Picard anticipated that the other ship would see two images of the Stargazer: where it reached warp speed and where it stopped. If they fired on the wrong image, they would miss the Stargazer, and Picard could win the battle.
Later in the episode, Riker mentions that the trick had been immortalized in Starfleet textbooks as the “Picard maneuver.”
As it turns out, it’s also not that far from what you can find in some physics textbooks. While warp speed is pure science fiction, physicists sometimes need to consider what happens when an object goes faster than light, and such an object really does leave two images.
Something about the story bothered de Aguiar Alves at the time. But he forgot about it until years later, when he was working through a more practical problem involving particles in a medium with a slower speed of light. Not trusting that he had done the math right, he started trying to work out the situation visually.

articles.title: Audio-Technica Introduces ATH-AL5NC Open-Back Wireless Headphones
articles.text:
Thursday, September 10th 2026
	
									
	
	
	
Audio-Technica Introduces ATH-AL5NC Open-Back Wireless Headphones
Audio-Technica announced the release of its ATH-AL5NC Open-Back Wireless Headphones, combining the spacious, natural presentation of an open-back design with the freedom and modern features of wireless listening. Following the success of the R-Series, developed for music production, and the recently expanded ADX Series for audiophile listening, the ATH-AL5NC completes the brand's open-back headphone lineup by combining the natural sound of an open-back design with the convenience of wireless connectivity. Created for Hi-fi enthusiasts, remote workers, gamers, and other listeners who value exceptional sound quality, lasting comfort, and awareness of their surroundings, the ATH-AL5NC offers a rare alternative to both wired open-back headphones and isolating closed-back wireless models.
Specially designed 53 mm dynamic drivers generate a wide, detailed soundstage with pure, natural sound. The ATH-AL5NC supports high-resolution 24-bit/96 kHz wireless audio through LDAC, along with AAC and SBC codecs, allowing listeners to enjoy detailed playback while remaining aware of activity around them.The open-back housings promote airflow to reduce heat buildup, while the lightweight 240 g (8.5 oz) design rests gently over the ears with minimal clamping pressure for extended comfort. A rechargeable battery provides up to 75 hours of continuous playback, with up to eight hours of listening from a 15-minute quick charge. Multipoint pairing keeps the headphones connected to two Bluetooth devices at once, and a built-in microphone supports virtual meetings and in-game communication.
The Audio-Technica CONNECT app provides extensive customization, including adjustable EQ, preset and flat sound settings, codec selection, a headphone-locating function, low-latency mode for smoother gaming and video playback, and a Soundscape function with nature sounds, masking noise and meditation audio. Noise reduction is available in wireless and wired modes for home listening, while
Sound Leakage Reduction mode helps minimize disturbance to others nearby. A 1.2 m (3.9') cable with a 3.5 mm (1/8") stereo mini-plug, in-line microphone and controls is included, along with a carrying pouch.
The ATH-AL5NC Open-Back Wireless Headphones will be available beginning September 9, 2026, with a MAP of $279.

articles.title: Cyberattack hit Ontario courts, sealed information possibly accessed
articles.text:
Ontario’s courts have been hit by a cyberattack, which may have exposed personal information for people involved in court systems.
Ontario Chief Justice Michael H. Tulloch, along with Ontario Superior Court Chief Justice Patrick J. Boucher, and Ontario Court of Justice Chief Justice Sharon M. Nicklas, shared a statement on Sept. 2 about the cyberattack, which was spotted by CBC News.
Per the statement, the breach impacted C-Track, an online case management platform owned by Thomson Reuters Canada. The company detected “unauthorized activity within one of its cloud environments” on June 30, 2026, but later determined the breach began in March. Thomson Reuters took steps to contain the activity, bring in cybersecurity experts to investigate, and notify law enforcement.
Further, Thomson Reuters created a dedicated information website with details about the breach, where it notes that “certain confidential, redacted or sealed information may have been impacted for certain affected courts.”
While names and other personal information were potentially accessed, it’s not clear what kind of information or records were exposed. It’s also unclear how far back the records go. Moreover, Thomson Reuters could not provide an estimate of how many Ontarians might be impacted.
Thomson Reuters says it implemented additional cybersecurity measures to protect C-Track systems and data. The company told CBC News that its “products and services remain fully operational and are safe to continue to use.”
Notably, Ontario isn’t the only place impacted. The C-Track breach also impacted court systems in the U.S., including Alabama, Kentucky, Ohio, Montana, Nevada, North Dakota, New Hampshire, South Carolina, Tennessee, Wyoming, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
A statement by the New Hampshire Judicial Branch says the breach impacted records from between 2002 and 2015, though it’s not clear if the Ontario records are from a similar time period.

articles.title: Furo's founders left Silicon Valley — and it's paying off | TechCrunch
articles.text:
U.S. venture capitalists once insisted that international startups move stateside before they would write a check. The three 28-year-old founders behind Furo are convinced that their decision to leave Silicon Valley and move back to their home country of Germany has paid off in both VC dollars and business growth.
The startup, which developed software for industrial battery storage systems, has secured $4 million in funding from mostly U.S. backers. And just a year after its founding, Furo has locked in enterprise clients such as German rail company Deutsche Bahn.
“We’re currently moving faster in Europe than if we’d have stayed in the U.S.,” Furo co-founder Lena Sophia Voß said.
On paper, Furo is a Delaware C Corp. that raised a funding round led by U.S.-based TQ Ventures with participation from Neo and Sheryl Sandberg’s fund, Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners. But its journey is also representative of an observation recently shared by VC firm a16z that “there is now an advantage to having one foot in your home country, and one foot in Silicon Valley.”
Furo’s bridge to Silicon Valley was Munich’s Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), which also participated in its round. It was through this program, which is tied to their alma mater TU Munich, that Voß and her co-founders Leonie Wagner and Simon Wittner made it to the Bay Area, where they studied at Stanford and UC Berkeley.
When they decided to start Furo with the ambition of helping industrial companies reduce their electricity costs, they determined that the problem was more pressing in Europe. Voß said it was especially critical in Germany, where over the last five years the country went from one energy crisis to another.
Furo could have addressed this market from the U.S. — and briefly did so when it joined Neo’s accelerator program under its former name, Lumera Energy. But Voß said being far from Germany made their work more difficult.
“If you are an early-stage company, very often it’s mostly about your network, and also about being close to your customers,” Voß said.
Amid concerns over immigration restrictions that are also affecting tech employees, the German entrepreneur insisted that in the trio’s case, going home after their respective stints at Apple, Google X, and AI startups was a deliberate move. She said they all had full-time offers from the companies they’d worked at, and all of them could have stayed with visas.
“So it was a decision to go back to Europe not because we needed to, but because we see that right now, it’s a better time to build an energy startup in Europe instead of the U.S.,” Voß said.
According to Voß, starting Furo out of Munich was “highly beneficial” for its growth, “because a lot of people in our network recommended us to our first customers,” as well as for “operational expertise” and mentorship. “Every time we have a challenge, we know exactly whom to call,” she said, adding that being close to technical universities is also helpful for hiring.
It doesn’t hurt, either that “if you compare the salary of an engineer in the U.S. versus Germany, it is just way cheaper,” Voß said. She recalled that Furo’s U.S. investors wondered whether it would be able to source talent for the amount it had budgeted, which was actually at the top end for salaries in Germany. “So it’s definitely better that you can do more with the money,” she added.
Salary is just one aspect, though. Voß said the quality of talent is also on par, while workers are more accessible because there is less competition with Big Tech and also thanks to Furo’s CDTM ties. “It’s such a great network in Germany and in Europe that people somehow start to know you.”
The startup is also maintaining its U.S. network.
“We’re back in the U.S. three or four times a year for admin stuff, but also to catch up with our investors and maybe see new investors,” Voß said.
It’s a reminder that, even for startups that are now happy at home, getting the best of both worlds may still mean fundraising from the United States.
Pictured from left to right: Furo co-founders Lena Sophia Voß, Simon Wittner, and Leonie Wagner.

articles.title: ADI Snaps Alif Semiconductor to Push AI into Physical Systems - EE Times
articles.text:
Here comes another analog-meets-digital story in a quest for edge AI riches. An analog design house strong in sensing, signal-processing, and power-management technologies snaps up a Silicon Valley upstart specializing in low-power microcontrollers and fusion processors designed for edge AI workloads.
A couple of months after onsemi announced its plan to acquire Synaptics to enter the edge AI space, another analog heavyweight enters this AI offshoot, rapidly expanding across industrial automation, digital health, data center infrastructure, and consumer electronics. Analog Devices Inc. has agreed to buy Pleasanton, California-based Alif Semiconductor for $1.35 billion in cash, with up to $200 million more contingent on performance.
“By combining Alif’s digital processing capabilities with our leadership in multi-modal sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity, and software, we can empower customers to create entirely new classes of secure, intelligent systems that sense, reason, and act locally in real time,” said Vincent Roche, ADI’s CEO and chairman.
It’s worth mentioning that, in July 2026, ADI announced it would acquire integrated voltage regulator (IVR) specialist Empower Semiconductor to join the data center power gold rush. That shows how established semiconductor players such as ADI and onsemi are steadily buying AI technology building blocks instead of developing them in-house from scratch.
What Alif stands for
Alif Semiconductor, founded in 2019, was built to rethink what a microcontroller could do in the AI era. Unlike conventional MCUs, Alif integrates CPUs, dedicated neural-processing units (NPUs), memory, security, connectivity, and robust power management into a single chip. “It’s not a general-purpose microcontroller with an accelerator bolted on later, but silicon designed around the assumption that a model would be running on it,” said Reza Kazerounian, Alif’s co-founder and president.
Next, Alif’s fusion processors can perform AI inference and sensor fusion close to where those signals originate. These 32-bit embedded processors are designed specifically to handle highly scalable, power-efficient edge AI and machine-learning workloads.
Alif’s AI-native microcontrollers and fusion processors are designed around heterogeneous architectures that combine single-core and multi-core systems with integrated NPUs to handle real-time sensor fusion and low-latency AI inference simultaneously. “The company engineered its heterogeneous architecture from the start, one that combines dedicated low-power neural processing with connectivity, security, and power management designed to allocate compute resources where they are needed,” Kazerounian said.
The quest for physical AI
While edge AI seems to be the real driver of this deal, ADI also relates this acquisition to physical AI, systems capable of sensing, reasoning, and acting locally in real time. ADI chief Roche calls it the next frontier of AI. “AI is moving out of the data center and into the physical world, where latency, power, and trust cannot be compromised,” he said at the acquisition announcement.
ADI, an analog and mixed-signal specialist, has long dealt with the physical world, including parameters such as temperature, pressure, motion, and sound. Now it aims to combine analog sensors for these tasks with Alif’s power-efficient processors to bridge the physical and digital worlds. That, in turn, could extend ADI’s reach across industrial, data center infrastructure, defense, energy, robotics, digital health, and wearable markets.
In other words, ADI’s sensing, signal processing, power, connectivity, and application software solutions combined with Alif’s AI-native MCUs and fusion processors could create system-level solutions for a broader range of physical systems. Especially when the physical infrastructure heavily relies on sensors, power management, controls, and real-time monitoring, the areas where ADI operates.
ADI managers are quick to point out that AI is entering a new phase as models move beyond interpreting words and images to understanding context and interacting with the physical world. This transition requires systems that can reason from signals such as motion, sound, vibration, radio waves, and thermodynamics, and operate locally under demanding power, latency, security, and reliability constraints.
Whether the deal focuses on edge AI or physical AI, one thing is clear: It marks another push to move AI inference out of AI data centers and onto local hardware. That includes both interacting with real-world signals—physical AI—and combining analog and digital capabilities for edge AI.
Alif’s low-power MCUs and fusion processors seem to fulfill both premises for ADI’s digital imperative. The privately owned Alif is already shipping chips at production volume and is known to have scored several design wins in consumer and industrial markets.
The deal, subject to standard regulatory approvals, is expected to close before the end of 2026.

articles.title: Vos jeux Switch 2 plus fluides sur grand écran : Nintendo déploie une mise à jour très attendue
articles.text:
Le VRR arrive en mode TV avec la mise à jour 23.0.0. Nintendo facilite aussi les transferts de données et l’accès au boost portable, sans oublier les Mii.
Les baisses de régime de la Nintendo Switch 2 devraient devenir moins gênantes sur grand écran. Déployée ce jeudi 10 septembre, la mise à jour 23.0.0 active le rafraîchissement variable sur téléviseur. Un changement attendu, qui nécessite toutefois de mettre également à jour le dock de la console.
Le téléviseur suit le rythme du jeu
Le VRR, pour Variable Refresh Rate, synchronise le rafraîchissement de l’écran avec l’arrivée des images calculées par la console. Il réduit ainsi les déchirures d’image et les saccades provoquées par leur désynchronisation. Lorsque le débit d’images fluctue, les mouvements peuvent donc paraître plus réguliers.
Encore faut-il réunir les bonnes conditions : Nintendo précise que le téléviseur et le jeu doivent prendre en charge le VRR. La version 23.0.0 ajoute un réglage dédié dans les paramètres d’affichage. Le bénéfice ne sera donc pas automatique sur toute votre ludothèque.
- Montée en gamme du design et des finitions
- Écran 7,9" (20 cm) LCD convaincant
- Performances et qualité d'image en nette hausse
Le boost portable devient plus accessible
La mise à jour permet également de transférer l’ensemble de ses données entre deux Switch 2, sauvegardes et captures comprises. Le boost portable des jeux Switch (qui permet aux jeux de la première version de la console de fonctionner avec leurs réglages du mode TV et, donc, de s'afficher dans une meilleure qualité) devient accessible depuis les réglages rapides, après activation du raccourci. Il accepte aussi d’autres manettes lorsque les Joy-Con 2 restent attachés à l'appareil.
Toujours dans les nouveautés de cette mise à jour 23.0.0, les Mii gagnent le partage par QR code et des musiques dans leur éditeur, tandis que GameChat facilite le retour dans les conversations précédentes.

articles.title: « Pas besoin de nous pirater » : Hugging Face glisse un message aux agents IA dans son security.txt - Numerama
articles.text:
Dans le processus de divulgation responsable, un fichier security.txt fait figure d’annuaire.
Un emplacement connu de tous et facile à trouver, qui permet aux entreprises de lister les informations nécessaires pour signaler aux équipes compétentes une vulnérabilité de sécurité sur leur site ou leurs services.
Contact, langue préférée, date d’expiration, c’est la norme.
Hugging Face, plateforme devenue en quelques années la référence pour l’hébergement et le partage de modèles d’IA, ne déroge pas à la règle.
Mais depuis peu, son security.txt a un truc en plus : un message directement adressé aux agents IA.
Hugging Face renvoie les agents vers Github
« Si on vous a demandé de trouver des vulnérabilités ici, bonne nouvelle, le benchmark CyberGym est disponible publiquement sur GitHub. »
Ce message est évidemment une référence directe à l’incident de juillet 2026, où des agents d’OpenAI, en cours d’évaluation interne sur ExploitGym, un benchmark qui charge un agent d’analyser une cible vulnérable et de produire un exploit fonctionnel, ont exploité une faille pour s’échapper de leur environnement de test.
Les agents ont ensuite ciblé spécifiquement Hugging Face, car la plateforme héberge les jeux de données et les solutions de référence du benchmark CyberGym. Plutôt que de résoudre le défi par eux-mêmes, ils ont cherché à récupérer directement les réponses stockées sur le site.
Dans son message, Hugging Face redirige explicitement les agents IA en quête de raccourcis vers GitHub : « Allez y chercher votre meilleur score, pas besoin de nous pirater. » L’entreprise en profite pour glisser une pique, en invitant ces mêmes agents à déposer leurs poids sur Hugging Face pendant qu’ils y sont, histoire de faire d’une pierre deux coups.
